Bacterial_Leaf_Blight.quote: The first signs of rice with bacterial leaf blight are water-soaked lesions at the edges and towards the tip of leaf blades.
In seedlings, infected leaves turn grayish-green and roll up. As the disease progresses, leaves turn yellow and wilt.

Bacterial_Panicle_Blight.quote: Symptoms include straw-coloured panicles with discoloured florets and darker basal portion of the glumes, and the panicles remain upright due to partially or aborted grain filling.
Typical symptoms of plants infected with B. glumae include browning of panicles, aborted seeds, empty grains as a result of failure of grain filling, brown spots on panicles, and seedling rot.

Blast.quote: oval or diamond-shaped leaf lesions with pointed ends and greyish or white centres, up to 1 cm long on younger plants but up to 2 cm long on plants at flowering, with dark green or reddish-brown margins sometimes with a yellow halo
Infected nodes turn blackish-brown and become shrunken, which can lead to lodging of the plant as the stem weakens at the infected node.
Infection of the basal node of the panicle causes "neck rot", with infected nodes appearing dark and dry, and often resulting in the stem breaking.

Brown_Spot.quote: The characteristic symptoms of brown spot on leaves and glumes include light reddish-brown lesions or lesions with a gray center surrounded by a dark to reddish-brown margin, and then by a bright yellow halo.
Neck and panicle infection causes chaffy and shriveled grains, and the panicles dry up and break down when the seed is ripening.

Leaf_Blight.quote: The first symptom of the disease is a water soaked lesion on the edges of the leaf blades near the leaf tip. The lesions expand and turn yellowish and eventually grayish-white.

Leaf_Smut.quote: The characteristic sign of rice with leaf smut is the presence of small black spots on the leaves that are slightly raised and angular and give the leaves the appearance of having been sprinkled with ground pepper.

Sheath_Blight.quote: The first symptom is an oblong, water-soaked lesion on leaf sheaths at or near the water line.
The symptoms of ShB primarily develop on leaf sheaths and leaf blades.

Tungro.quote: Yellow or orange-yellow discoloration is noticeable in tungro-infected plants, with discoloration beginning from the leaf tip and extending down to the blade or the lower leaf portion.
The disease causes leaf discoloration, stunted growth, reduced tiller numbers and sterile or partly filled grains.
